headline: Almost half of UK GP practice managers surveyed say patients' AI-written complaints, some 20 pages long, are adding to workload and hurting staff morale.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: the story is fresh (11 Oct 2026) and the facts match the headline, but it rests on one small UK survey.
importance_line: AI makes it quick for patients to write long, formal complaints, which may slow replies and pull practice staff away from patient care, but the evidence is one survey of nearly 160 managers run by a body that advises doctors, so the scale of the problem is not measured.
summary: The Independent reports, citing a survey by the Medical Protection Society (MPS), which gives legal and indemnity advice to health workers, that only 7 percent of nearly 160 UK practice managers have never received an AI-generated complaint and 45 percent say such complaints add to workload and damage morale. The MPS says the letters can run to 20 pages with occasionally questionable legal arguments and may divert time from patient care, while the Royal College of GPs says complaints still matter for accountability but AI can make them needlessly long or inaccurate.
notes: The pool item (GPonline) returned 403, so the text was read on The Independent (11 Oct 2026) and cross-checked against LBC, whose text is near-identical (possibly shared agency copy, not confirmed). Survey method and dates are not given.
